newsitem.title: USA: Gun dealer says McVeigh wanted detonating cord.
newsitem.headline: Gun dealer says McVeigh wanted detonating cord.

text.p: A gun dealer testified Thursday in the trial of Timothy McVeigh that the accused Oklahoma City bomber tried to buy detonating cord in the months before the deadly blast.
Detonating cord is a critial ingredient in certain types of bombs.
The dealer, Greg Pfaff, said he met McVeigh several times at gun shows where, not long before the bombing, McVeigh told him he needed detonating cord "badly."
The dealer, the prosecution's first witness of the day, said he told McVeigh he would try to find him the cord but never did.
McVeigh was accused of building and setting off the huge fertiliser-based truck bomb on April 19, 1995, at the Alfred P. M urrah federal building in Oklahoma City that killed 168 people.

Wednesday's testimony concluded with a mining engineer who gave the anonymous jury a primer on how a bomb made of ammonuim nitrate and fuel oil would explode and where its ingredients could commmonly be purchased.
